subject: math
cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
intro: Divide using the standard long-division algorithm. Carry out the divide-multiply-subtract-bring-down cycle for each digit, place every quotient digit correctly, and express any remainder. Where it helps, check your answer with $\text{quotient} \times \text{divisor} + \text{remainder} = \text{dividend}$.

steps: $15 \div 6 = 2$ with $3$ left over, since $6 \times 2 = 12$ and $15 - 12 = 3$. Write $2$ over the $5$.
Bring down the $1$ to make $31$. $31 \div 6 = 5$ with $1$ left over, since $6 \times 5 = 30$ and $31 - 30 = 1$. Write $5$.
Bring down the $2$ to make $12$. $12 \div 6 = 2$ with $0$ left over. Write $2$.
The quotient is $252$ with remainder $0$.
Check: $252 \times 6 = 1{,}512$. Correct.
$8 \div 7 = 1$ with $1$ left over, since $7 \times 1 = 7$ and $8 - 7 = 1$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $6$ to make $16$. $16 \div 7 = 2$ with $2$ left over, since $7 \times 2 = 14$ and $16 - 14 = 2$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $1$ to make $21$. $21 \div 7 = 3$ with $0$ left over. Write $3$.
The quotient is $123$ with remainder $0$.
Check: $123 \times 7 = 861$. Correct.
$24 \div 4 = 6$ with $0$ left over. Write $6$ over the second $4$ of the dividend.
Bring down the $0$ to make $0$. $0 \div 4 = 0$. Write $0$ in the quotient.
Bring down the $8$ to make $8$. $8 \div 4 = 2$ with $0$ left over. Write $2$.
The quotient is $602$ with remainder $0$. Notice the $0$ in the tens place of the quotient.
Check: $602 \times 4 = 2{,}408$. Correct.
$30 \div 5 = 6$ with $0$ left over. Write $6$.
Bring down the $7$ to make $7$. $7 \div 5 = 1$ with $2$ left over, since $5 \times 1 = 5$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $5$ to make $25$. $25 \div 5 = 5$ with $0$ left over. Write $5$.
The quotient is $615$ with remainder $0$.
Check: $615 \times 5 = 3{,}075$. Correct.
$58 \div 8 = 7$ with $2$ left over, since $8 \times 7 = 56$ and $58 - 56 = 2$. Write $7$.
Bring down the $3$ to make $23$. $23 \div 8 = 2$ with $7$ left over, since $8 \times 2 = 16$ and $23 - 16 = 7$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $2$ to make $72$. $72 \div 8 = 9$ with $0$ left over. Write $9$.
The quotient is $729$ with remainder $0$.
Check: $729 \times 8 = 5{,}832$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm and express any remainder: $4{,}379 \div 7$.

steps: $43 \div 7 = 6$ with $1$ left over, since $7 \times 6 = 42$ and $43 - 42 = 1$. Write $6$.
Bring down the $7$ to make $17$. $17 \div 7 = 2$ with $3$ left over, since $7 \times 2 = 14$ and $17 - 14 = 3$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $9$ to make $39$. $39 \div 7 = 5$ with $4$ left over, since $7 \times 5 = 35$ and $39 - 35 = 4$. Write $5$.
No digits remain, so the leftover $4$ is the remainder. The quotient is $625\text{ R }4$.
$21$ does not go into $7$, so look at $76$. Estimate $76 \div 21 \approx 3$. $21 \times 3 = 63$ and $76 - 63 = 13$. Write $3$.
Bring down the $4$ to make $134$. Estimate $134 \div 21 \approx 6$. $21 \times 6 = 126$ and $134 - 126 = 8$. Write $6$.
Bring down the $4$ to make $84$. $84 \div 21 = 4$ exactly, since $21 \times 4 = 84$. Write $4$.
The quotient is $364$ with remainder $0$.
Check: $364 \times 21 = 7{,}644$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm and express any remainder: $4{,}827 \div 23$.

steps: $23$ does not go into $4$, so look at $48$. $48 \div 23 = 2$, since $23 \times 2 = 46$ and $48 - 46 = 2$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $2$ to make $22$. $23$ does not go into $22$, so write $0$ in the quotient and bring down the next digit.
Bring down the $7$ to make $227$. Estimate $227 \div 23 \approx 9$. $23 \times 9 = 207$ and $227 - 207 = 20$. Write $9$.
No digits remain, so the leftover $20$ is the remainder. The quotient is $209\text{ R }20$. The $0$ in the tens place is essential.
$6 \div 3 = 2$ with $0$ left over. Write $2$.
Bring down the $0$ to make $0$. $3$ does not go into $0$, so write $0$ in the quotient.
Bring down the $1$ to make $1$. $3$ does not go into $1$, so write $0$ in the quotient. (These interior zeros must be written.)
Bring down the $8$ to make $18$. $18 \div 3 = 6$ with $0$ left over. Write $6$.
The quotient is $2{,}006$ with remainder $0$. Check: $2{,}006 \times 3 = 6{,}018$. Correct.

items.prompt: A baker has $3{,}458$ muffins and packs them into trays that each hold $24$ muffins. How many full trays can the baker fill, and how many muffins are left over?
items.answer: $144$ full trays with $2$ muffins left over

steps: Set up the division $3{,}458 \div 24$.
$24$ does not go into $3$, so look at $34$. $34 \div 24 = 1$, since $24 \times 1 = 24$ and $34 - 24 = 10$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $5$ to make $105$. Estimate $105 \div 24 \approx 4$. $24 \times 4 = 96$ and $105 - 96 = 9$. Write $4$.
Bring down the $8$ to make $98$. Estimate $98 \div 24 \approx 4$. $24 \times 4 = 96$ and $98 - 96 = 2$. Write $4$.
The quotient is $144\text{ R }2$. So the baker fills $144$ full trays with $2$ muffins left over. Check: $144 \times 24 + 2 = 3{,}456 + 2 = 3{,}458$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm and express any remainder: $52{,}614 \div 37$.

steps: $37$ does not go into $5$, so look at $52$. $52 \div 37 = 1$, since $37 \times 1 = 37$ and $52 - 37 = 15$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $6$ to make $156$. Estimate $156 \div 37 \approx 4$. $37 \times 4 = 148$ and $156 - 148 = 8$. Write $4$.
Bring down the $1$ to make $81$. $81 \div 37 = 2$, since $37 \times 2 = 74$ and $81 - 74 = 7$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $4$ to make $74$. $74 \div 37 = 2$ exactly, since $37 \times 2 = 74$. Write $2$.
The quotient is $1{,}422$ with remainder $0$. Check: $1{,}422 \times 37 = 52{,}614$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm and express any remainder: $61{,}205 \div 48$.

steps: $48$ does not go into $6$, so look at $61$. $61 \div 48 = 1$, since $48 \times 1 = 48$ and $61 - 48 = 13$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $2$ to make $132$. Estimate $132 \div 48 \approx 2$. $48 \times 2 = 96$ and $132 - 96 = 36$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $0$ to make $360$. Estimate $360 \div 48 \approx 7$. $48 \times 7 = 336$ and $360 - 336 = 24$. Write $7$.
Bring down the $5$ to make $245$. Estimate $245 \div 48 \approx 5$. $48 \times 5 = 240$ and $245 - 240 = 5$. Write $5$.
No digits remain, so the leftover $5$ is the remainder. The quotient is $1{,}275\text{ R }5$. Check: $1{,}275 \times 48 + 5 = 61{,}200 + 5 = 61{,}205$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm: $73{,}108 \div 26$. Then check your answer with $\text{quotient} \times \text{divisor} + \text{remainder} = \text{dividend}$.

steps: $26$ does not go into $7$, so look at $73$. $73 \div 26 = 2$, since $26 \times 2 = 52$ and $73 - 52 = 21$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $1$ to make $211$. Estimate $211 \div 26 \approx 8$. $26 \times 8 = 208$ and $211 - 208 = 3$. Write $8$.
Bring down the $0$ to make $30$. $30 \div 26 = 1$, since $26 \times 1 = 26$ and $30 - 26 = 4$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $8$ to make $48$. $48 \div 26 = 1$, since $26 \times 1 = 26$ and $48 - 26 = 22$. Write $1$.

items.prompt: A factory produces $84{,}330$ bolts and ships them in crates of $65$ bolts each. Every crate must be completely full to ship. How many full crates can be shipped, and how many bolts remain in the warehouse?
items.answer: $1{,}297$ full crates with $25$ bolts left over

steps: Set up the division $84{,}330 \div 65$.
$65$ does not go into $8$, so look at $84$. $84 \div 65 = 1$, since $65 \times 1 = 65$ and $84 - 65 = 19$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $3$ to make $193$. Estimate $193 \div 65 \approx 2$. $65 \times 2 = 130$ and $193 - 130 = 63$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $3$ to make $633$. Estimate $633 \div 65 \approx 9$. $65 \times 9 = 585$ and $633 - 585 = 48$. Write $9$.
Bring down the $0$ to make $480$. Estimate $480 \div 65 \approx 7$. $65 \times 7 = 455$ and $480 - 455 = 25$. Write $7$.
The quotient is $1{,}297\text{ R }25$. Only full crates ship, so $1{,}297$ crates are shipped with $25$ bolts left over. Check: $1{,}297 \times 65 + 25 = 84{,}305 + 25 = 84{,}330$. Correct.

items.prompt: Divide using the standard algorithm and express any remainder: $90{,}450 \div 43$. Watch for an interior $0$ in the quotient.

steps: $43$ does not go into $9$, so look at $90$. $90 \div 43 = 2$, since $43 \times 2 = 86$ and $90 - 86 = 4$. Write $2$.
Bring down the $4$ to make $44$. $44 \div 43 = 1$, since $43 \times 1 = 43$ and $44 - 43 = 1$. Write $1$.
Bring down the $5$ to make $15$. $43$ does not go into $15$, so write $0$ in the quotient. (This interior $0$ must be recorded.)
Bring down the $0$ to make $150$. Estimate $150 \div 43 \approx 3$. $43 \times 3 = 129$ and $150 - 129 = 21$. Write $3$.
No digits remain, so the leftover $21$ is the remainder. The quotient is $2{,}103\text{ R }21$. Check: $2{,}103 \times 43 + 21 = 90{,}429 + 21 = 90{,}450$. Correct.
